transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-26
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~1h8m
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Ethan Lin (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood Solutions), Tom Baker (Redwood CSM), Olivia Chen (BlueCartel Head Procurement), Ravi Patel (BlueCartel Legal), Diego Morales (CTO), Sara Klein (FinOps), Martin Ruiz (Security)

Auto Summary (inline): Quick MSA/DPA triage, pricing clarifications for Dedicated, KMS/privileged keying discussion, pilot scope and timing.

Topics Covered: see metadata list above

Action items (inline): see metadata action_items for owner/due dates

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Thompson: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we know folks are spread across regions so appreciate the time. Quick roll call, and we'll jump into MSA redlines and then pricing scenarios.
[00:14] Olivia Chen: Thanks, Maya. We got a tight procurement window — goal is to move vendor selection by mid April so want to understand if Redwood can support our KMS/privileged key requirements and whether that changes pricing or SLA.
[00:29] Ethan Lin: Totally. We'll do a two-track: legal routing and tech validation. From se side, the main items that change infra/pricing are private VPC vs hosted, dedicated reserved capacity, and any privileged key or egress fee structures.
[00:45] Ravi Patel: On the MSA side I'm mostly focused on indemnity, data handling and the DPA alignment — we have a region residency requirement for EU data and an auditor who wants proof of key custody. Also curious about retention windows, logs, and audit export.
[01:03] Maya Thompson: Understood. Quick note — we can provide a redacted MSA that shows our standard KMS language and an appendix for on-prem / private deployment. I will send that with tracked changes.
[01:18] Diego Morales: From an engineering angle, we need to know whether Redwood's Dedicated nodes can be pinned to a specific kernel/quant profile — we have long context prompts and smaller p99 latency needs.
[01:34] Ethan Lin: Yes, Dedicated supports model pinning and quant profiles. Also prefix KV caching is supported but note that in some places the runtime will swap to a quantized path; there's an optimization tradeoff between latency and token cost. Sorry — that's a mouthful.
[01:50] Priya Rao: (soft) And we can include an operations appendix describing how rollouts and canary policies work in Dedicated and Private.
[02:05] Sara Klein: Will pricing for Dedicated include egress per GB? Our finance team is very sensitive to egress costs.
[02:15] Tom Baker: Good question. Typical structure is base reserved capacity fee + per-token usage for overage + optional egress fees depending on the VPC/router arrangement. For many enterprise customers we include an egress allowance in the committed tier and then tiered per-GB over that.
[02:33] Olivia Chen: Okay, procurement wants to see a clear example: say 40 nodes reserved for three months with 5 TB egress per month, what's the total street price — that kind of thing.
[02:44] Maya Thompson: We'll produce a pricing scenario spreadsheet with those line items. I'll add example SLOs too so procurement can see latency/availability guarantees.
[02:55] Martin Ruiz: On security — is Redwood able to integrate with our HSM for key wrapping or do we need a redwood-managed KMS? Also where are audit logs retained and can we push them to our Splunk?
[03:10] Ethan Lin: We support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own) via standard KMS integrations — that allows customer key wrapping. Audit logs can be forwarded via an ingestion endpoint; we also support push to S3 or direct syslog that you can pick up with Splunk. Caveat: For on-prem / air-gapped setups there are additional steps and lead time.
[03:30] Ravi Patel: Regarding DPA, we have an internal requirement for 7 year log retention for certain transaction types — is that feasible?
[03:40] Maya Thompson: Retention windows are configurable in enterprise tiers; long-term retention may have an archival fee. We'll call that out in the pricing example.
[03:52] Olivia Chen: On routing for the MSA — legal wants to understand the escalation lane if an exception is needed. Who signs off on DPA exceptions, is there a standard addendum?
[04:06] Maya Thompson: Typically exceptions are routed through our contracts team; small exceptions can be approved by our AE with legal sign-off, more material changes hit a contract escrow review. We'll map that and give you a contact list.
[04:20] Ravi Patel: Also want to confirm whether Redwood will accept our custom data processing terms or if you insist on your template. Some of the indemnity language is a sticking point.
[04:33] Maya Thompson: We can accept certain customer terms; we'll highlight the non-starters in the redline and propose alternative wording for indemnity and warranty. If needed, we can escalate to legal for a 1:1.
[04:47] Diego Morales: Back to technical — for the pilot perf test, what environment will we use? Hosted or Dedicated? We prefer Dedicated to get realistic throughput/latency but if that's not available we can accept a hosted equivalence.
[05:02] Ethan Lin: For a realistic pilot we recommend a short Dedicated slot — we can spin up a single reserved node for your test prompts; it'll reflect tail latency and token economics better than hosted, especially since you have long contexts.
[05:18] Olivia Chen: Cost for that pilot? Procurement won't approve anything that looks like open-ended spend.
[05:25] Maya Thompson: We usually do a time-boxed pilot with a capped cost line item; Redwood will propose a pilot quote that covers the reserved node for the test window plus a token cap. We'll add that to the spreadsheet.
[05:40] Sara Klein: On billing and approval lanes — we need an invoice-friendly breakdown: committed vs variable, egress lines, privileged keying add-on. Can you provide sample invoice lines?
[05:52] Tom Baker: Yes we'll produce sample invoice rows. We can also include suggested GL coding for finance.
[06:00] Martin Ruiz: A note about privileged access: for certain flows we need vault-based ephemeral keys and RBAC at the token level. Can Redwood provide token-level RBAC and audit traceability?
[06:15] Ethan Lin: Token-level RBAC is in our roadmap; we can provide role-based API keys and detailed audit logs today. For ephemeral keys and Vault integration we have patterns we've implemented with customers — we can share the ops playbook.
[06:32] Ravi Patel: On escrow — procurement may request source escrow for certain regulated transactions. Does Redwood have an escrow path?
[06:40] Maya Thompson: We have an escrow partner and can discuss terms; typically source escrow is for very large enterprise deals and requires separate contract. We'll note that as a potential escalation.
[06:52] Olivia Chen: Timeline recapping: procurement decision mid-April. Legal review — we'd like redlined MSA back by the end of next week. Pilot run week of April 6. Is that feasible?
[07:05] Maya Thompson: Yes, timeline is feasible. We'll aim to get docs to Ravi by Mar 30 and the Dedicated pilot scheduled for Apr 6.
[07:14] Olivia Chen: Great.
[07:18] --- mid-call, deeper legal exchange (small gaps, some cross-talk) ---
[25:00] Ravi Patel: (speaking quickly) A couple of specific redline points — limitation of liability cap tied to fees is okay but want carve-outs for gross negligence and data breaches; also want clarity on subprocessor lists and 3rd party subprocessors.
[25:20] Maya Thompson: We'll propose a compromise: carve-out language for gross negligence and will provide subprocessor list with 30 day notice for changes.
[25:34] Ravi Patel: For breach notification windows we need 72 hours max.
[25:40] Maya Thompson: Redwood standard is 72 hours for security incidents; we'll commit to that in the DPA.
[25:48] Diego Morales: Technical note — can logs be filtered to exclude PII before forwarding to customer Splunk? We don't want regulated fields sent outside.
[25:58] Ethan Lin: Yeah we have log masking and can do pre-forwarding filters, but you'll need to provide a schema or field map to apply filters reliably.
[26:12] Martin Ruiz: Also, what about data residency for EU-only customers? If we serve EU customers from EU region do you offer guaranteed routing?
[26:22] Priya Rao: We offer region routing policies and can pin requests to regionally placed nodes; however, in multi-region failover we have documented fallback rules. We'll include the routing policy in the appendix.
[26:36] Olivia Chen: A couple of procurement-specific asks: sample SLA credits calculation, the approval chain for exceptions, and an example of the change-control process for on-prem deployments.
[26:48] Maya Thompson: Noted — we'll include sample SLA credit calc, exception routing matrix, and change-control template in the annex.
[27:00] --- end of deeper legal sections ---
[45:12] Ethan Lin: Quick perf test plan: SE will take your top 20 prompt templates, we will run those against a single Dedicated node configured to your model choice, measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost. We will share raw logs and a one-page summary.
[45:29] Diego Morales: We also want KV cache behavior explained — there was a mention earlier of prefix caching, how much improvement should we expect for our workload?
[45:38] Ethan Lin: With prefix caching you'd often see 20-40% token cost reduction on repeated prompts and up to 15% p95 latency improvement depending on pattern. but results vary — we'll quantify in the perf run.
[45:53] Olivia Chen: On the MSA signatory — who at Redwood signs enterprise MSAs? We need a procurement-level contact.
[46:01] Maya Thompson: Our Legal Director signs enterprise MSAs; I'll include name and contact in the redline package.
[46:09] Ravi Patel: If we highlight three non-starters in the redline, what's the turnaround on negotiation? We need clarity so procurement can plan meetings.
[46:20] Maya Thompson: For up to three material redlines we can usually turn around within 3-5 business days; more complex items may be a week or more if they require exec legal involvement.
[46:33] Olivia Chen: Perfect.
[46:36] --- closing and recap section ---
[55:00] Maya Thompson: OK recap: Redwood to send redacted MSA + DPA with proposed alternate indemnity language; Redwood to produce Dedicated pricing scenario with egress lines and pilot quote; SE to run perf test and share results; customer to circulate internal stakeholders and confirm procurement window.
[55:19] Olivia Chen: I'll get stakeholder list to Maya and cc Ravi.
[55:25] Ravi Patel: I'll review the redline and flag non-starters by Mar 30.
[55:31] Ethan Lin: I'll schedule the Dedicated pilot slot and run the perf tests week of Apr 6, share raw logs and summary.
[55:40] Maya Thompson: Great — we'll send calendar invites for the pilot and follow-up. Thanks everyone.
[55:50] Diego Morales: Thanks.
[56:00] Tom Baker: Noted — I'll prepare sample invoice lines.
[56:08] Martin Ruiz: Thanks all.
[56:12] Maya Thompson: Meeting adjourned.

Post-call notes (AE): Legal asked specifically for 72 hour breach notification, subprocessor list with 30 day notice, escrow as escalation, and BRL-like indemnity language are potential sticking points. Procurement wants an example invoice with GL codes and a capped pilot quote. SE will run perf run on Dedicated.

References shared in call:
- Link: redwood.io/enterprise/msadpa (redacted demo link)
- Pricing spreadsheet: (will be shared)
- Ops playbook: ops.redwood/privileged-keys-playbook (internal)

End of transcript.
